title: Sales Enablement: Unified Playbook - Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Mehta
content:
Overview
------
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's go-to-market messaging, competitive briefs, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance, customer case study template, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this as the single source of truth for AE/SE enablement when evaluating fit, preparing decks, or responding to security and pricing questions.

Intended audience
- Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Solutions Architects, Sales Leadership, and Customer Success for entitlement/expansion conversations.

Owners and escalation
- Primary owner: Go-to-market Enablement (Aisha Mehta)
- Security reviewers: Security & Compliance (Michael Chen)
- Complex pricing approvals: Revenue Ops (Sofia Alvarez)
- Escalation path: AE -> SE -> Go-to-Market Lead -> Product/Security as needed (see "Escalation checklist" below).

1) High-level positioning and one-liners
-------------------------------------
Core positioning (one-liner): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, economical, and reliable LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Elevator pitch (15-30s):
- "Redwood lets engineering teams deploy LLMs with production-ready performance - predictable latency and unit cost, unified tooling across hosted and private deployments, and built-in fallbacks to keep apps online.
- We combine a GPU-optimized runtime, smart routing, and observability so engineering teams ship faster without operating a custom serving stack."

Persona-tailored messaging
- Product/Engineering lead: Focus on latency SLOs, deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private), and observability traces for debugging regressions.
- Platform/Infra lead: Emphasize dedicated capacity, autoscaling controls, network/VPC options, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs.
- Security/Compliance lead: Highlight private control plane option, SOC/ISO controls, data residency, and audit evidence processes.
- Business/POC sponsor: Focus on fast time-to-value, cost per 1M tokens, and predictable SLA for production traffic.

Messaging pillars (talking points)
- Production-first: SLA-backed Dedicated option, runtime with batching and KV cache, and graceful degradation policy.
- Unified experience: Same API and rollout controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Cost-aware controls: Batching, quantization profiles, and routing policies that reduce per-token cost.
- Observability & guardrails: Token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and regression alerts against eval sets.

2) Competitive brief template and key battlecards
------------------------------------------------
Use this template when preparing a competitor comparison for an opportunity. Save completed battlecards in the opportunity folder in CRM.
- Competitor: [Name]
- Positioning summary: 1-2 sentences
- Typical customer profile: (size, industry, workloads)
- Strengths: 3 bullets
- Weaknesses / risks: 3 bullets
- Differentiators (Redwood): 3 bullets with evidence (benchmarks, features)
- Pricing & contracting considerations: (how they price, common discount patterns)
- Common objections and rebuttals: 5 Q/A pairs
- Win themes / use-case angles to prioritize: 3 bullets

Examples (high-level)
- Competitor: Managed LLM Vendor X
  - Positioning: Simple hosted API + closed models.
  - Strengths: Fast sign-up, curated closed models, bundled data labeling.
  - Weaknesses: No private deployment, limited observability, unpredictable cost at scale.
  - Redwood differentiators: Dedicated capacity with SLA, private deployment, token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
  - Rebuttal example: "If you need private hosting or predictable throughput, Redwood's Dedicated and Private options reduce operational overhead while maintaining unit economics."

3) Pitch deck guidance and slide-by-slide notes
------------------------------------------------
Use the following canonical slide structure for an initial 20-25 minute prospect deck (customize to buyer persona):
1. Title slide: Logo, speaking AE/SE, date, one-line value prop.
2. Agenda: 3-5 bullets.
3. Customer problem: Brief bullets on production inference pain points (cost, latency, reliability, ops).
4. Redwood overview & value prop: One-liner + 3 pillars (performance, economics, ops).
5. How it works (high level): Serving runtime, smart routing, caching & batching, deployment modes.
6. Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (one slide or split into three).
7. Performance evidence: Latency/throughput benchmarks, quantization profiles, and example token latency numbers (include sample graphs).
8. Observability & guardrails: Console screenshot and bullet list of dashboards and alerts.
9. Security & compliance: Data residency, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and relevant certifications.
10. Pricing & packaging: Summary tiers, reserved capacity examples, and negotiation levers.
11. Case study: 1 customer (problem, solution, metrics).
12. Deployment & timeline: POC steps, success criteria, and typical 30/60/90 day plan.
13. Next steps & ask: Trial, technical deep dive, procurement info.

Presentation tips for SEs
- Start with clarifying questions about volume, latency SLOs, data residency, and failure modes.
- Use concrete numbers: e.g., 95th/99th percentile token latency, tokens/sec per GPU estimate, unit cost per 1M tokens.
- Avoid deep infra jargon unless the audience asks; focus on outcomes for product and infra stakeholders.

Slide artifacts to keep updated
- Performance benchmarks (CSV/PNG), Console screenshots, Sample SLOs and runbook excerpt, Security one-pager.

4) Pricing guidance and negotiation levers
--------------------------------------
Keep pricing simple in early-stage conversations. Use Revenue Ops for custom proposals. Always capture competitive pricing intelligence in CRM.

Public starter guidance (example numbers for conversation only - consult Revenue Ops):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $0.03 per 1K prompt tokens, $0.06 per 1K completion tokens, Embeddings $0.01 per 1K vectors.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Monthly commit starting $10k/month for small pool; typical mid-market $50k-150k/month for predictable throughput. Includes baseline SLA.
- Private/On-prem: Platform fee + professional services; typical minimum $200k/year for on-prem engagements.

Common discount and contracting levers
- Commitment length (12/24/36 months)
- Reserved throughput (tokens/sec or GPUs)
- Professional services / onboarding fee (can be reduced for strategic deals)
- Observability retention tiers (add-on)
- Premium SLAs and enterprise support (add-on)

Pricing table (reference, include in slides)
- Tier | Typical ARR / Monthly commit | Key includes
- Starter | $0 (or small trial credits) | Hosted API, basic quotas
- Business | $10k-50k/mo | Reserved capacity option, standard SLA, enhanced observability
- Enterprise | $50k+/mo or custom | Private deployments, KMS/HSM, audit evidence, premium SLA

Approval thresholds
- Discounts > 25% require Revenue Ops approval.
- Custom contract terms or data residency clauses require Legal and Security review.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for sales teams)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Hosted: customer data is stored in region selected at onboarding; default retention is 30 days for logs, 365 days for audit records. Private: data remains in customer VPC or on-prem. We provide data retention settings during provisioning and support custom retention via contract.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. Private deployments support KMS integration and HSM-backed keys. For Dedicated we support BYOK integrations with major cloud KMS providers.

Q: Can we run Redwood in a VPC or air-gapped environment?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. Review our on-prem checklist for pre-reqs.

Q: What certifications and audits do you have?
A: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation for our control plane. For Private deployments we provide evidence packages and support customer audits.

Q: How do you prevent data leakage between customers?
A: Multi-tenant hosted environments use strict namespace isolation, network segmentation, and RBAC. Dedicated and Private options provide physical/logical isolation; all KV caches and model artifacts are namespaced per customer.

Q: Do you log or use customer prompts to train models?
A: No. We do not use customer prompts or outputs to train or improve models unless explicitly authorized in writing by the customer.

Q: What is your incident response and notification process?
A: We follow our incident response runbook: initial notification within 60 minutes for Sev-1 incidents, a public status-page with updates, and a post-incident report within 7 business days. We provide customers with direct contacts for contractual incidents.

Q: What access controls and audit logging are available?
A: RBAC, SCIM/SSO integration (SAML/OIDC), and detailed audit logs that record API calls, config changes, and admin actions. Logs can be exported to customer SIEM.

Q: How do you support data residency requirements?
A: We offer region-specific hosting and Private deployments. For strict residency customers we recommend Private with on-prem or dedicated region-only deployments.

For technical deep dives and full security packs, request the Security One-Pager or contact Security & Compliance (security@redwood.ai).

7) Sales motion playbooks (short)
--------------------------------
Inbound qualification (AE)
1. Clarify use case and critical success metrics (latency SLO, daily tokens, peak tokens/sec).
2. Identify stakeholders: product engineer, infra lead, security/compliance.
3. Recommend initial POC path (hosted trial, dedicated pilot, or private eval) and collect required capacity numbers.
4. Introduce SE for technical scoping.

Outbound ABM / Strategic logo (AE+SE)
1. Use account research + persona mapping.
2. Lead with production pain (cost spikes, unpredictability) and Redwood differentiator (Dedicated + Private).
3. Run a targeted 4-6 week pilot with defined success criteria.

POC / Pilot checklist (SE)
- Success criteria (clear metric): e.g., 99th pct latency <= X ms, monthly token cost <= $Y, integration within 2-4 weeks.
- Baseline metrics captured pre-POC.
- POC plan: data, endpoints, model variant, test harness, monitoring collection.
- Backup plan: fallback model variant and timeout policy.

8) Appendix: objection handling snippets
--------------------------------------
Objection: "We can just build this ourselves."
- Reply: "Many teams start there. Building a production-ready serving platform requires repeatable observability, cost controls, and ongoing kernel/runtime tuning across model versions. Redwood provides those building blocks off-the-shelf and reduces time-to-market and total cost of ownership."

Objection: "We're concerned about vendor lock-in."
- Reply: "Redwood emphasizes standard APIs and supports model pinning and export of configuration. For Private deployments, customers control their infrastructure and keys."
